t: Dim the lights in the evening: use lamps instead of ceiling lights from about 3 hours before bed.

t: Have your last caffeine at least 6 hours before bed; for a standard coffee, about 9 hours.

t: If you nap, keep it short (about 10–20 minutes) and in the afternoon.

t: Keep your bedroom comfortably cool: adjust the heating, open a window or use a fan, and change bedding with the seasons.
ref: Okamoto-Mizuno, K., & Mizuno, K. (2012). Effects of thermal environment on sleep and circadian rhythm. t: Make your bedroom dark: close the curtains or blinds, cover standby lights, and try an eye mask if light still gets in.

t: Cut bedroom noise: close windows on the noisy side, move away from noise sources, or try foam earplugs.
ref: Basner, M., & McGuire, S. (2018). WHO Environmental Noise Guidelines for the European Region: A systematic review on environmental noise and effects on sleep. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health, 15(3), 519. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph15030519

t: Warm up before exercise with light activity, then movements like the ones you're about to do.
ref: Fradkin, A. J., Zazryn, T. R., & Smoliga, J. M. (2010). Effects of warming-up on physical performance: a systematic review with meta-analysis. t: Build in lighter days between harder sessions, and increase training gradually (keep weekly increases under about 30%).
ref: Nielsen, R. Ø., Parner, E. T., Nohr, E. A., Sørensen, H., Lind, M., & Rasmussen, S. (2014). t: Turn on step counting on your phone and check your daily average.
ref: Bravata, D. M., Smith-Spangler, C., Sundaram, V., Gienger, A. L., Lin, N., Lewis, R., Stave, C. D., Olkin, I., & Sirard, J. R. (2007). Using pedometers to increase physical activity and improve health: a systematic review. JAMA, 298(19), 2296–2304. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.298.19.2296

t: Use music you enjoy during workouts; save faster tracks for harder efforts.
ref: Terry, P. C., Karageorghis, C. I., Curran, M. L., Martin, O. V., & Parsons-Smith, R. L. (2020). Effects of music in exercise and sport: A meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin, 146(2), 91–117. https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000216

t: Turn off non-essential notifications, and use Do Not Disturb while you focus.
ref: Kushlev, K., Proulx, J. D. E., & Dunn, E. W. (2016). "Silence Your Phones": Smartphone Notifications Increase Inattention and Hyperactivity Symptoms. In Proceedings of the 2016 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (pp. 1011–1020). ACM. https://doi.org/10.1145/2858036.2858359
